units.titles: Whitelisting in queuing contract can be bypassed by directly queuering the storage contract
units.known_address_notes: Oak Security audit (2022-02-08) of OnePlanet NFT marketplace: repo scope https://github.com/ProjectOnePlanet/{auction-contracts,contract-queuing,contract-token} — all now 404. OnePlanet ran on Polygon (later Terra migration noted in press). Wayback has no snapshot of the repos or docs.oneplanet.io; Polygon Blockscout search API returns 403 and Etherscan V2 has no contract-name search, so the queuing/storage contract pair named in the finding could not be located.

OtterSec report (2026-04-27) on Onrail's Solana private-credit programs (RTL/loan state, PoolMgmtOps, Vault, NFT collateral). Identity confirmed: onrail.xyz, GitHub org 'Onrail'. The org publishes only ts-sdk (generic amount/binary-layout/svm utilities, no IDL or program IDs) and no docs site; the audited programs are private. No program address published anywhere.

units.titles: The contract can be drained completely, and attackers can pay in esoteric currencies
units.known_address_notes: Oak Security audit (2024-01-27) of an Anchor/Solana program; scope repo https://github.com/stephanOUT/rust-contract at commit 0e2cc8f239669493189f5fbdabe7c78f4b40d7f3 (finding 'toggle_trading ...'). Both repo and org (stephanOUT) are 404 now; the report contains no program ID and the front-end/project site is unknown, so no on-chain program could be verified.
